instructions_for_claude: This is an UPDATE to the Curriculum AI presentation you already made, not a new deck. Keep the existing deck, its theme, layouts and every slide not mentioned below. Apply only the changes in 'changes', in order. Six new screenshots are attached; their file names match the 'screenshots' section. Style the new slide and the new screenshots exactly like the existing ones (same browser-window frame, callout style, colours, eyebrow labels and fonts). Slides are referred to by their current title, with their number in the original 13-slide outline in brackets in case titles were edited; if a slide has moved, find it by title and content. Do not invent figures. Put talking points in speaker notes. When done, list every slide you changed.
what_changed_in_the_app: Sign-in: people sign in with a link emailed to them. No passwords. Only people on the pilot's members list get a link, and the sign-in page gives everyone the same reply so it can't be used to find out who has access.

One account per person, one view per role: a student, a lecturer or a Head of Department sees only their own view. The role switcher in the top bar is gone; the top bar now shows the person's role, name and a Sign out button.
Each student's data is private to them: their chats, progress and questions. The lecturer sees the class, anonymised by student number.
Lecturer dashboards now count the real signed-up students (marked ● Live) alongside a 30-student synthetic class, labelled as such, while the pilot is small.

The demo student is now Eric M. (student number STR-2024-0117), replacing Sara Kamau. He starts from the same sample progress, so every figure in the deck still holds (Depreciation 38%, rising to 54% after a correct practice answer).
The 'Reset demo' button is gone, because with real accounts it would wipe students' work.

screenshots.shows: The sign-in page: Curriculum AI logo on deep navy, 'Sign in' card with one email field and an 'Email me a sign-in link' button. Text: no password needed.
After asking for a link: 'Check your email' with the address entered (eric.m@strathmore.edu). The same message shows whether or not the email has access.

Eric M. signed in as a student: top bar with a blue 'Student' badge, his name and Sign out; sidebar with his courses and 'Curriculum AI suggests' Depreciation 38%; Curriculum AI's welcome 'Hi Eric'; progress panel at 56% with the gaps Curriculum AI has spotted.

The lecturer signed in (top bar: teal 'Lecturer' badge, 'Muray Innovations · SBS 201 · Financial Accounting', Sign out). Class overview with the line 'Class: 1 signed-up student, whose activity updates these figures live, plus 30 synthetic students while the pilot is small', KPI cards, heatmap and the default session brief.

Individual students, with Eric's row (STR-2024-0117, ● Live, Today, 66%, On track) highlighted, and his detail panel: per-topic mastery from Depreciation 38% to Accounting equation 92%, and Curriculum AI's recommendation to push Depreciation next.
Someone who signs in but isn't on the pilot list (guest@example.com) sees 'No access yet' and a Sign out button.
